title: Surjective coefficient-extension map for a complete local power-series presentation
statement: Let $F,K$ be fields and $\iota:F\hookrightarrow K$ a field embedding. Let $(R,\mathfrak m_R)$ and $(C,\mathfrak m_C)$ be nonzero commutative Noetherian local rings [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], complete and separated for their maximal-ideal-adic topologies [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring]. Fix residue-field identifications $R/\mathfrak m_R=F$, $C/\mathfrak m_C=K$ and ring sections $\sigma:F\to R$, $\tau:K\to C$ of the residue maps. Let $h:R\to C$ be a continuous local ring homomorphism, meaning $h(\mathfrak m_R)\subseteq\mathfrak m_C$, with $\mathfrak m_RC=\mathfrak m_C$ and $h\sigma=\tau\iota$. For integers $n,s\geq0$, fix a continuous surjective $F$-algebra map $\phi:F[[t_1,\ldots,t_n]]\to R$ for the action $\sigma$, with kernel $I=(f_1,\ldots,f_s)\subseteq(t_1,\ldots,t_n)$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. Let $j:F[[t_1,\ldots,t_n]]\to K[[t_1,\ldots,t_n]]$ apply $\iota$ to every coefficient, put $I_K=(j(f_1),\ldots,j(f_s))$ and $T=K[[t_1,\ldots,t_n]]/I_K$, and write $\pi:K[[t_1,\ldots,t_n]]\to T$ for the quotient map. There is a continuous surjective $K$-algebra map $\Psi:K[[t_1,\ldots,t_n]]\to C$ satisfying $\Psi(t_i)=h(\phi(t_i))$ and $\Psi\circ j=h\circ\phi$. It annihilates $I_K$ and induces a surjective $K$-algebra map $\theta:T\to C$ with $\theta\pi=\Psi$. The ring $T$ is Noetherian local with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_T=(\pi(t_1),\ldots,\pi(t_n))$ and residue field $K$. There is a local map $\alpha:R\to T$ uniquely specified by $\alpha\phi=\pi j$, and $\theta\alpha=h$. One has $\mathfrak m_RT=\mathfrak m_T$; under the residue identifications $T/\mathfrak m_RT=K=C/\mathfrak m_RC$, the reduction of $\theta$ is the identity of $K$.

source.place: Tag 0C54 (lemma-base-change-complete-local-ring), variable generation, power-series map, surjectivity, transported relations and commutative quotient square; abstracted to compatible complete local rings.

proof.text: Put $P_F=F[[t_1,\ldots,t_n]]$, $P_K=K[[t_1,\ldots,t_n]]$ and $\mathfrak a_L=(t_1,\ldots,t_n)\subset P_L$. By [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-local-ring], $P_F$ is local and its maximal ideal consists of series with zero constant coefficient; [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-combined-ideal-coefficients] with base ideal zero and exponent $1$ identifies this ideal with $\mathfrak a_F$. Since $\phi$ is surjective, $\phi^{-1}(\mathfrak m_R)$ is maximal, hence equals $\mathfrak a_F$. Thus $\phi(\mathfrak a_F)=\mathfrak m_R$ and the elements $b_i=h(\phi(t_i))$ generate $\mathfrak m_RC=\mathfrak m_C$.

source.place: Tag 0C54 (lemma-base-change-complete-local-ring), proof: variable generation, power-series surjection and commutative quotient square.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-coefficient-field-generator-presentation] with field $K$, ring $C$, its given residue identification and section $\tau$, and generators $b_i$. Its hypotheses hold by Step 1 and completeness and Noetherianity of $C$. It supplies a continuous surjective $K$-algebra map $\Psi:P_K\to C$ with $\Psi(t_i)=b_i$.

source.place: Tag 0C54 (lemma-base-change-complete-local-ring), proof: variable generation, power-series surjection and commutative quotient square.

proof.text: The coefficientwise map $j$ is a ring map by the finite Cauchy product formula of [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. It takes $\mathfrak a_F^N$ into $\mathfrak a_K^N$, so it is continuous. The continuous maps $\Psi j$ and $h\phi$ agree on variables and on constants, since $h\sigma=\tau\iota$. Apply the uniqueness assertion of [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-adic-evaluation] with coefficient ring $F$, target $C$, ideal $\mathfrak m_C$, coefficient map $\tau\iota$ and variables $b_i$. It gives $\Psi j=h\phi$ on all series.

source.place: Tag 0C54 (lemma-base-change-complete-local-ring), proof: variable generation, power-series surjection and commutative quotient square.

proof.text: For each relation, $\Psi(j(f_a))=h(\phi(f_a))=0$. Hence $I_K\subseteq\ker\Psi$. Define $\theta(\pi(g))=\Psi(g)$; this is well-defined, is a $K$-algebra map, and is surjective because $\Psi$ is. Also $I\subseteq\ker(\pi j)$: every $f_a$ maps to zero and these generate $I$. Define $\alpha(\phi(g))=\pi(j(g))$. Equality of two representatives differs by $I$, proving well-definedness, and surjectivity of $\phi$ proves uniqueness and $\theta\alpha=h$.

source.place: Tag 0C54 (lemma-base-change-complete-local-ring), proof: variable generation, power-series surjection and commutative quotient square.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-noetherian], $P_K$ is Noetherian. Every ideal of $T$ is generated by the images of generators of its inverse image in $P_K$, so $T$ is Noetherian. Each $j(f_a)$ has constant coefficient zero, so $I_K\subseteq\mathfrak a_K$. The constant coefficient map therefore descends to a surjection $T\to K$ with kernel $\pi(\mathfrak a_K)$, using [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-combined-ideal-coefficients] with base ideal zero and exponent $1$. A class outside this kernel has a representative with nonzero constant coefficient, which is a unit by [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-local-ring]; its class is a unit. Thus the kernel is the unique maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_T=(\pi(t_1),\ldots,\pi(t_n))$, and $T/\mathfrak m_T=K$.

source.place: Tag 0C54 (lemma-base-change-complete-local-ring), proof: variable generation, power-series surjection and commutative quotient square.

proof.text: Step 1 shows that $\mathfrak m_R$ is generated by $\phi(t_i)$, whose images under $\alpha$ are $\pi(t_i)$. Consequently $\alpha(\mathfrak m_R)\subseteq\mathfrak m_T$ and $\mathfrak m_RT=\mathfrak m_T$. Thus $\alpha$ is local. Since $\theta(\pi(t_i))=b_i\in\mathfrak m_C$, $\theta$ descends modulo these maximal ideals. For each $c\in K$, the constant class $\pi(c)$ represents $c$ in $T/\mathfrak m_RT$ and $\theta(\pi(c))=\tau(c)$ represents the same $c$ in $C/\mathfrak m_RC$. Every residue class has such a representative, so the reduced map is $\operatorname{id}_K$.
